THE PROBLEM WE’RE CRACKING

Food left behind.
Value left on the table.

The Heist’s Sustainability and Food challenge asks how we can reduce food waste and the cost, water, and carbon tied to it. Our starting point is the campus cafe: food is already made, shelves are still stocked, and the selling day is running out.

We’re exploring a simple connection between inventory, responsible price changes, and a menu that makes the opportunity visible. Students find a better-priced bite. Cafes get a clearer way to move surplus.

OUR DIRECTION

A smaller footprint. A more accessible meal.

These are goals for a future pilot, not measured results.

01 / FOOD

Less unsold food.

Help cafes sell appropriate surplus before their approved selling window ends. Track sales, retained stock, transfers, and discards separately.

02 / ACCESS

More affordable choices.

Show the price, the saving, and what’s available. Keep minimum prices and protected stock under the cafe’s control.

03 / RESOURCES

Make the impact count.

Evaluate waste reduction first. Add water and carbon estimates only with a documented method and a credible comparison.

HOW THE EXCHANGE WORKS

Count. The cafe enters its food, stock, and menu prices.

Review. Eligible batches are checked against the pricing rules.

Connect. Confirmed offers reach the case, TV, and mobile menu.

    Food & inventory

    OFFER REVIEW

    Find a responsible price.

    Demo checkout

    Choose a batch and check its offer. If a lower price passes the checks, publish it to every screen. A hold keeps the current price. Each batch gets one decision; newly received food is a separate batch.

    Evaluate to inspect candidate prices, expected gain, and downside. No recommendation changes the screen before acknowledgment.

    Advanced assumptions & stock set aside

    These are explicit prototype assumptions, not validated cafe economics or demand. Selling fee 0%; incremental sale cost $0.20; fixed-order fee $0; activation cost $0.25; minimum contribution $0.25. Terminal value −$0.05/unit. Scenario weights 30%/40%/30%, including weak response, capacity limits, and outside displacement. No real checkout is connected.

    Defaults: 0/15/30/45% ladder; $0.50 minimum gain; $0 downside allowance; strict positive sales uplift; 120-minute review; 5-minute fulfillment buffer; 30-minute inventory age. One committed decision per batch/window.

    04 / THE DEAL DESK

    Give the offer a story.

    Build a food pairing, review bakery surplus, or run a last-call review. Price drops still need to pass the pricing checks. A pairing adds its two confirmed item prices; it does not create an extra discount.
